claim: The trustees of the BAE Systems Pension Scheme and BAE Systems Executive Pension Scheme publicly appointed Goldman Sachs Asset Management to manage approximately £23bn of UK DB assets; Goldman announced it by press release.
passage: BAE Systems Pension Schemes Trustees Appoint Goldman Sachs Asset Management for Approximately £23 Billion UK Pension Schemes Mandate
notes: The BAE relationship is public, not confidential: the former intern's description of it as confidential does not apply to the existence of the mandate. Fees, terms and internal detail remain non-public.

claim: BAE Systems' in-house investment management team joined Goldman Sachs Asset Management as part of the mandate.
passage: BAE Systems' in-house investment management team will join Goldman Sachs Asset Management.
notes: P&I (2025) names the in-house entity as BAE Systems Pension Funds Investment Management. The number of people is not public. This is one appointment; it does not show that every OCIO deal absorbs the client's team.

claim: The BAE appointment followed a competitive tender; Redington advised the trustees, Travers Smith acted as trustees' lawyers and PwC advised the sponsor.
passage: highly competitive tender process
notes: Adviser names are from Professional Pensions, not the press release.

claim: GSAM remained the BAE Systems Pension Scheme's OCIO in the scheme year to 31 March 2026, with Gallagher as the trustee's separate investment adviser.
passage: the day-to-day management of the Scheme's investments is carried out by GSAM, the Scheme's OCIO
notes: Scheme's own implementation statement. SIPs 'were last updated on 11 July 2024 to reflect the appointment of Goldman Sachs Asset Management International'.

claim: Goldman described the BAE mandate as the largest OCIO mandate awarded in the UK to that date.
passage: Press release and trade reports (S01, S02, S03); wording varies by outlet
notes: A self-description repeated by trade press; comparison deals cited are BA/BlackRock (about £21.5bn, 2021) and Centrica/Schroders (£10bn, 2022).

claim: No public source read links Goldman Sachs Asset Management to the Jaguar Land Rover pension schemes; the schemes' own annual reports name Willis Towers Watson as fiduciary manager.
passage: FIDUCIARY INVESTMENT MANAGER Willis Towers Watson Limited
period: Years ended 31 March 2024 (Land Rover Pension Scheme) and 31 March 2025 (Jaguar Pension Plan)
notes: Full text of both reports was searched for 'Goldman' and 'GSAM': no occurrences. The Jaguar Pension Plan report also names Hymans Robertson as investment consultant and says 'The return seeking and CDI portfolios are managed by Willis Towers Watson on a delegated basis'. A change after 31 March 2025 cannot be excluded, but none was found. The former intern's statement is an Unverified account and conflicts with the latest public documents. Do not name JLR as a Goldman client in interview material.

claim: Various Shell pension entities and a captive insurer appointed GSAM to a $40bn OCIO and investment advisory mandate, including about $15.6bn in the UK and $2.8bn in Germany.
passage: various pension entities and a captive insurance company related to Shell Plc and its subsidiaries
notes: Amounts are plan assets covered, not fees. Remaining assets are not itemised by country.

claim: The Shell appointment followed a competitive tender overseen by Isio, with each fund making its own decision.
passage: follows a competitive tender process, overseen by Isio
notes: Shell said it acted as coordinator only.

claim: Goldman's Shell press release quotes Chloe Kipling as co-head of EMEA Institutional Client Coverage at Goldman Sachs Asset Management.
passage: Press release (S08) attribution line: Chloe Kipling, co-head of the EMEA Institutional Client Coverage at Goldman Sachs Asset Management
notes: Public use of the phrase 'Institutional Client Coverage' as a business name in EMEA. It does not by itself establish what 'CCG' means internally or that coverage equals relationship management. Title wording is as extracted from the fetched release; check the exact wording on the page before quoting.

claim: Shell's Dutch pension fund (SSPF) is not part of the Goldman mandate; it appointed BlackRock in 2024.
passage: Professional Pensions and ai-CIO reports (S09, S10)
notes: Shows that group schemes choose providers separately.

claim: Goldman has reported global OCIO assets under supervision of more than £200bn (Sept 2023, no as-of date), nearly $450bn (Sept 2025, no as-of date) and $480bn as of 31 March 2026.
passage: $480 billion in OCIO assets under supervision
notes: Figures are from separate press releases with different currencies and, for two of them, no as-of date. P&I reports $311.8bn OCIO AUM at 31 Dec 2024 (S07). Do not compute growth rates from mixed bases without stating them.

claim: GSAM was appointed fiduciary manager for two schemes in the Short Brothers Common Investment Fund (£1.6bn) after a tender supported by PwC.
passage: Following a rigorous process, we concluded that Goldman Sachs Asset Management offered a solution
notes: Ed Francis quoted as managing director and head of UK fiduciary management.

claim: The £240m Calor Group Retirement Benefits Plan appointed GSAM as fiduciary manager, replacing Cardano, after a tender overseen by Barnett Waddingham.
passage: The day-to-day management of the Plan's assets is currently delegated to Cardano Risk Management Limited
notes: Passage is from the plan's statement for the year to 5 April 2024 and confirms the incumbent; the appointment itself is from Professional Pensions.

claim: The Northern Foods Pension Scheme trustees appointed GSAM as their new fiduciary manager after 31 March 2025.
passage: we've appointed Goldman Sachs Asset Management (GSAM) as our new Fiduciary Manager
notes: Scheme value £645.5m at 31 March 2025; assets managed by GSAM, date and predecessor not stated.

claim: The £360m Sun Chemical Pension Scheme mandate (2015), taken from Mercer, was reported as GSAM's first publicly announced UK fiduciary appointment.
passage: Professional Pensions, 26 June 2015 (S20), opening paragraph

claim: Team transfers are a feature of some large OCIO deals (BAE, UPS, Bombardier; some Shell staff) but are not reported for the smaller UK fiduciary appointments (Short Brothers, Calor, Northern Foods, Sun Chemical).
passage: Comparison across S01, S04, S07, S11, S15, S16, S19
notes: Absence of a reported transfer is not proof that none occurred; smaller schemes rarely have in-house investment teams to transfer.

claim: Part of GSAM's OCIO scale came from acquisitions and liftouts (Pacific Global Advisors 2015, Verus OCIO business 2017, Aptitude 2018, Bombardier team 2022).
passage: Institutional Investor, 7 September 2023 (S04)
notes: Single trade source.

claim: UPS appointed GSAM as OCIO for US and Canadian DB plans holding $43.4bn at 31 March 2024; a 22-person investment team joined GSAM on 1 September 2024.
passage: we (were) only a team of 22 including me when we moved over

claim: Goldman announced over $70bn of retirement mandates from Verizon and Lockheed Martin, split into $30bn DB assets under management and $40bn DC assets under advisement.
passage: $30 billion in defined benefit ("DB") OCIO assets under management ("AUM") for Verizon and Lockheed Martin and $40 billion in defined contribution ("DC") assets under advisement
notes: Passage is the Goldman release text as quoted in the search result; the fetched release confirmed the same figures and labels. AUM and AUA are not the same and should not be added together as 'managed assets'.

claim: Goldman Sachs completed the €1.7bn acquisition of NN Investment Partners in April 2022; more than 900 employees joined and GSAM's European AUS rose to more than $600bn.
passage: The TRADE, 11 April 2022 (S39)

claim: The NN IP deal came with a ten-year strategic partnership under which GSAM manages NN Group's portfolio, reported at about $190bn in 2021 coverage and about $180bn in later coverage.
passage: Search-result passages from secondary coverage; primary release (S41) returned HTTP 403
notes: Two figures circulate. Primary Goldman or NN Group release still needs to be read.

claim: Mubadala and Goldman Sachs Alternatives signed a $1bn separately managed account to co-invest in Asia Pacific private credit.
passage: a $1bn separately managed account
notes: A capital amount to be deployed, not a fund close.

claim: PIF and GSAM signed a non-binding MoU for PIF to act as strategic anchor investor for new Saudi and GCC private credit and public equity strategies; no amount was disclosed.
passage: act as a strategic anchor investor
notes: Subject to regulatory and internal approvals. No launched fund found before the cutoff.

claim: QIA and Goldman Sachs signed an MoU under which QIA will target combined commitments of $25bn to GSAM-managed funds and co-investments.
passage: will target committing a combined total of $25 billion to funds managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management

claim: Sources describe the QIA figure differently: the joint statement says 'target'; a trade headline says 'Commits $25B'.
passage: remains subject to certain terms, conditions and deliverables
notes: Prefer the joint statement. Useful example of commitment versus target.

claim: A Goldman press release names an 'EMEA Third Party Wealth Business' and quotes Hilary Lopez as its head (April 2025).
passage: Press release (S31) attribution line: Hilary Lopez, Head of the EMEA Third Party Wealth Business, Goldman Sachs Asset Management
notes: Confirms 'Third Party Wealth' is a publicly used business name in EMEA. Current status of the title after April 2025 was not re-checked in this stream. Title wording is as extracted from the fetched release.

claim: GSAM launched active UCITS ETFs in Europe in 2025: fixed income first, then an active equity range starting with GQUS on 28 April 2025.
passage: Goldman Sachs Asset Management press release, 28 April 2025 (S31)
notes: January 2025 fixed income launch details (tickers, 0.25% TER) are from an unfetched source.

claim: GSAM raised more than $200m for its first private markets ELTIF (2023) and in March 2026 announced its first evergreen ELTIF 2.0 product within a G-Series of six evergreen funds.
passage: Goldman Sachs' first evergreen product under the ELTIF 2.0 regulation
notes: The 'over $8bn' European private credit evergreen figure includes leverage and unfunded commitments as of 4 March 2026.

claim: Goldman Sachs closed its acquisition of Innovator Capital Management on 2 April 2026, adding about $31bn of AUS and taking GSAM to about 240 ETFs and about $90bn of ETF AUS.
passage: Goldman Sachs Asset Management press release dated 3 April 2026 (S35)
notes: Price of about $2bn is from Reuters via a search result only.

claim: Goldman Sachs took a position of up to $1bn in T. Rowe Price alongside a strategic collaboration on public and private market solutions.
passage: Investment Week, 5 September 2025 (S37), headline and first paragraph
notes: Stake ceiling (3.5%) and mid-2026 product timing not verified on a fetched page.

claim: Goldman Sachs managed part of Border to Coast's emerging markets equity allocation as at March 2025 and no longer appeared on the Global Equity Alpha Fund factsheet from April 2026.
passage: these no longer appear on the April factsheet
notes: The 2023 appointment detail is from search-result passages; the 2025 and 2026 statements are from fetched articles. Termination and its reason are not confirmed by the pool.

claim: A Kent Pension Board paper of 4 September 2025 lists a recommendation to end fixed income mandates with Goldman Sachs, Schroders and CQS.
passage: Search-result summary of the council paper; document returned HTTP 403
notes: Recommendation only; outcome not confirmed. Needs reading of the committee minutes.

claim: Pensioenfonds Vervoer appointed GSAM as fiduciary manager in 2006 (€5.4bn) and terminated the then €7bn mandate in 2010, citing underperformance.
passage: GSAM did not produce any outperformance
notes: Historical. Retention is not guaranteed even for a whole-portfolio relationship.

claim: In November 2022 the SEC charged Goldman Sachs Asset Management, L.P. with ESG policies and procedures failures; GSAM paid a $4m penalty without admitting or denying the findings.
passage: SEC Press Release 2022-209
notes: US entity and US products; no equivalent European regulatory action was found (search limited).

claim: No public source read attributes any of these wins to a named London sales or relationship team; where people are named they are senior leaders or business heads quoted in the announcement.
passage: Review of all fetched announcements in this register
notes: Being quoted in a release shows who spoke for the business, not who originated the mandate.

claim: In every UK fiduciary or OCIO appointment in this register where a selection process is described, a third-party adviser ran or supported the tender (Redington, Isio, PwC, Barnett Waddingham).
passage: S02 (Redington), S08 (Isio), S15 (PwC), S16 (Barnett Waddingham)
notes: Four cases; not a statistic about the market. UK rules require competitive tendering for most first-time fiduciary management appointments, which is for the regulatory stream to source.

claim: No public evidence was found in this stream for: a GSAM sub-advisory mandate from St. James's Place; a GSAM appointment by a UK DC master trust; any Nordic mandate after 2001; a named third-party insurer general-account mandate in EMEA other than NN Group and the Shell captive; UK charity or endowment mandates.
passage: See search log in research/evidence/R7.md
